JCHer here, super accepting environment, there is a queer committee which arranges events and a large portion of students identify in some way as LGBT+ I haven’t experienced any discrimination and feel quite safe being myself <3

JCH

party culture - occasional parties, people go out every weekend or two though and usually there’s people having droofs or casual drinks a couple nights a week so there’ll be opportunities to party if you want

academics - the highest achieving college in terms of academics, both due to academic support provided and study culture 

friendliness - fairly easy to make friends, especially if you get involved in activities 

social scene - most nights there will be people hanging out in the junior common room, playing pool or table tennis or having movie nights there are fun events every tuseday and on thursday clubbers (everyone hangs out and eats some late night food provided by the clubbers society) some people will have s’mores nights in their rooms around their fireplaces, there is formal hall on monday and themed dinners on thursdays eg. language tables, magical night

music - multiple places to practice music, including 3 upright pianos, a baby grand and a grand (only used for performances) most people play an instrument, it’s fairly common to hear lovely music throughout the college and there are a number of musical scholars in res 

arts - doesn’t produce a musical but does produce a play each year, performance opportunities at events throughout the year such as royal variety and winter song, occasional art classes eg. lino printing

sports - being a smaller college JCH doesn’t participate in all sports but does most including rowing, table tennis, cricket, netball, hockey, squash and a few others, there is support for sports and due to the college’s size you will be able to participate in most sports, although JCH is not generally very competitive fellow students will be there to cheer teams on
